result.markdown:
For most small businesses, I'd shortlist **Dropbox Sign, DocuSign, PandaDoc and SignWell**\. The best choice depends on how many documents you send, how many people need access, and whether you need more than just signatures.

My overall recommendation is **Dropbox Sign for straightforward business signing**, with DocuSign as the stronger choice if you need a more comprehensive platform.

- Reusable contract templates

- Signing status tracking
- Audit trails
- Google Drive and Dropbox integrations

| Software | Best suited to | Ease of use |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Dropbox Sign | Everyday contracts | Excellent |
| DocuSign | Business workflows | Very good |
| PandaDoc | Quotes and proposals | Very good |
| SignWell | Budget-conscious businesses | Excellent |
| Adobe Sign | PDF-heavy businesses | Very good |


## Important if you're operating in Australia

Electronic signatures are generally recognised under Australian law, but requirements can vary depending on the document, applicable legislation and state or territory. Australia's Electronic Transactions Act 1999 provides for electronic signatures in most Commonwealth processes, subject to requirements and exceptions. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/legal-system/electronic-signatures-documents-and-transactions/electronic-signatures?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/legal-system/electronic-signatures-documents-and-transactions?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I'd look for\:

- A certificate or audit trail showing who signed and when.
- Secure document storage.
- Identity verification where appropriate.
- Automatic reminders.
- Templates for frequently used contracts.
- Easy downloading of completed, signed PDFs.
